subject: Uplift simulation and grace-period pathing for renewal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Moreno <lina@aventishealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uplift simulation and grace-period pathing for renewal

Hi Lina —

Following our call earlier this week, I ran a few uplift simulations against your current consumption profile to surface paths that keep monthly spend predictable during the Q4 surge you mentioned. High level options:

- Option A (staggered top‑up): smaller mid-contract add-on now, remainder at co-term with renewal. Low near-term cash impact, slightly higher blended unit price.
- Option B (ahead commit + grace): reserve a 20% uplift now, with a 60‑day grace usage buffer that lets you spike up to the uplift without immediate true‑up. Better latency/cost guarantees during peaks.
- Option C (burst credits): pay-as-you-go with surge credits for peaks; lowest commitment but higher unit costs.

I attached an "rdw-2387-uplift-scenarios.xlsx" spreadsheet with numbers for each option and a quick SLA/latency note. Can you confirm which path you want us to price formally? If useful, we can send a short amendment draft for legal to review (I can include a targeted grace‑period clause).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20‑min call.

—Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Moreno <lina@aventishealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aventis Health Procurement <procurement@aventishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Uplift simulation and grace-period pathing for renewal

Sean —

Thanks for the work and the spreadsheet. A couple of quick clarifying questions from our side before we loop in finance/legal:

1) For Option B (ahead commit + grace), do spikes consume against the uplift instantly or within the 60-day window? We need to understand how usage accounting appears on invoices.
2) Can the grace buffer be limited to specific models/hosts or is it account-wide? We only expect spikes for a small subset of workloads.
3) If we go with a staggered top‑up, what are the pro‑rata invoicing impacts for Q3 vs Q4?

We prefer to avoid an immediate large prepayment — finance would favor Option A if the blended rate can be improved slightly. Legal also asked whether Redwood can provide a one‑time SL A waiver for incidents that occur during clear maintenance windows.

Happy to do a short call tomorrow 10–10:30 ET if that helps.

—Lina
Head of Engineering Operations
Aventis Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Uplift simulation and grace-period pathing for renewal

Sean / Monica —

Quick internal note after Lina's questions:

- Account-level vs model-level buffer: we can scope the grace buffer to a model tag (e.g., "prod-critical") and only count those hosts toward the 60‑day window. That prevents Aventis from consuming other experimental workloads against the uplift.
- Invoicing: for Option B, spikes within the 60‑day window won't trigger immediate invoice true‑up; they will show as a usage balance that rolls into the next invoice period and is reconciled at co‑term. We should surface this clearly in the amendment ("usage window" language).
- Pro‑rata: Option A's mid-contract add-on will be invoiced pro‑rata from the effective date to the co‑term; Rachel to add a sample pro‑rata line in the spreadsheet (done).

Attached: rdw-2387-uplift-scenarios.xlsx (updated) — includes a model‑scoped grace example and the pro‑rata sample line. Also added a proposed one‑time SLA waiver item that legal may want to tack onto the amendment.

Recommend we price Option A with a 4% blended discount improvement if Aventis accepts a vendor credit in lieu of a deeper cash discount (credit applies to next invoice cycle). That keeps near-term cash impact low while giving them tangible economic upside.

If you agree, I can produce a one‑page amendment + a redlined clause for the grace buffer and the SLA waiver.

—Rachel
Director, Renewals 
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Moreno <lina@aventishealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aventis Health Procurement <procurement@aventishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Uplift simulation and grace-period pathing for renewal

Lina —

Appreciate the quick questions. Short answers up front:

• Spikes under Option B are covered by the 60‑day grace window and are accounted for against the uplift; reconciliation happens at co‑term (no immediate invoice true‑up).
• We can absolutely scope the grace buffer by model tag and limit to up to 10 host groups you nominate.
• For Option A pro‑rata, you'll see a line item prorated to the effective date; I've included a sample in the spreadsheet.

Proposal for next steps:
1) We price Option A with the 4% blended vendor‑credit improvement (credit applied to next invoice).
2) Draft a one‑page amendment with: the mid‑contract add‑on details, model‑scoped grace buffer, 60‑day window language, and a one‑time SLA waiver for scheduled maintenance incidents.
3) Send amendment to Aventis legal for review — we'll include a prefilled DocuSign link to accept.

I've created the amendment draft and pushed the DocuSign packet here: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/agreements/RDW-2387

If that sounds right, I can route to legal/procurement and cc your procurement mailbox. If you want the finance team to see the vendor‑credit math before legal, say the word and I'll include them on the next send.

Thanks —
—Sean

From: Lina Moreno <lina@aventishealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Aventis Health Procurement <procurement@aventishealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Uplift simulation and grace-period pathing for renewal

Sean / Rachel —

This approach looks reasonable. Procurement copied here — they asked for: 

- A short redline for the grace‑window clause (we've attached Aventis' standard redline in a separate email).
- Confirmation that the model tag scoping can be amended down to 5 host groups if needed.

We're fine to proceed with Option A + the 4% vendor credit, pending legal redline. Please send the amendment and the DocuSign packet to procurement@aventishealth.com and cc me. Also include the "aventis-grace-period-term-redline.pdf" (we'll send our redline in parallel).

I'll aim to have procurement/legal review by EOD Friday. If you can get the amendment into DocuSign today, that helps speed review.

Thanks —
—Lina
